(2009) report, Table 2 gives the frequent group's days since last ketamine use (n = 30) as 2 (SD 2.60); the bracketed values printed beside it, (1–14), are labelled a range, but many such values in this table cannot be ranges (card sc_morgan_2010b, reporting issues). The authors state that they could not verify the 24 hours without psychotropic drugs before testing with biological samples, because ketamine stays in urine for 1 to 2 days, and that the experimenters judged that no one appeared intoxicated. Editors' comparison: the 2009 paper gives 1.6 (SD 1.27), range 1–7, for the same session (its Table 2, p. 81).

evidence_set: Three days after a night of use, the ketamine group, which reported using ketamine from twice a week (12%) to once a month (12%), rated dissociation 17.75 (17.41) against 5.37 (7.21) (p<0.008) and state schizotypal symptoms 62.35 (25.35) against 26.42 (20.45) (p<0.001), with magical ideation 28.25 against 11.00, compared with peers with little or no ketamine use, whose scores correlated highly across the two days (r = 0.93 and 0.94), although their mean schizotypal score fell from 33.37 to 26.42; both scales rate the current state. Depression on the anxiety and depression questionnaire was 4.45 (2.11) against 1.89 (1.29) on the night, a rating that covered the previous two days, and 4.30 (2.58) against 1.68 (1.29) three days later (group F(1,32) = 19.4), which the authors call low and well below the clinically significant range of 8–11.

evidence_set: On day 3, 15 participants reported cannabis (8 in the more frequent and 7 in the less frequent group) and 12 alcohol (8 and 4; 1 to 3 units), without a statement of whether this came before the retest. The more frequent group rated more sedation than the less frequent group on both days (alertness factor, group F(1,35) = 4.63, p<0.04; the authors read higher scores as more sedation) and more nausea (group F(1,35) = 5.37, p<0.05); on day 3 it rated more impaired concentration, 33.11 (26.84) against 12.74 (12.53) (group × day F(1,35) = 5.79, p<0.025), and more impaired memory, 35.94 (23.09) against 15.42 (18.00) (a group effect printed with the same statistic, F(1,35) = 5.79).
